newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana deputy surrenders, frees hostages.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana deputy surrenders, frees hostages.

text.p: A Louisiana deputy sheriff surrendered on Friday, ending a 26-hour standoff that began after he shot a teller to death and took five people including his estranged wife hostage in a local bank, police said.
Chad Louviere, 24, could be charged with first-degree murder and kidnapping after allegedly shooting 27-year old Pamela Duplantis to death and holding several people hostage since early Thursday.
"The last two hostages including his ex-wife are unharmed and Chad Louviere surrendered without incident," a state trooper told Reuters.
The trooper said it was unclear what had triggered Louviere's actions. "I still don't know what he wanted. There were some marital problems involved, but I don't understand any of it," he said.
Louviere freed one hostage in exchange for lunch Thursday, traded a second at mid-afternoon for a two-way radio and released a third Thursday night as a good faith gesture, police said.
Louviere was also a suspect in a rape committed three hours before he entered the bank, police said.
The stand-off began after Louviere entered an ArgentBank branch where his estranged wife worked. He was on duty, armed and in uniform, police said.
Police surrounded the bank and blocked downtown streets with tractor-trailer trucks, which paralysed the business district of Houma, 45 miles southwest of New Orleans.
Louviere had been a deputy for only a few months but served three years as a city police officer in nearby Thibodaux, police said.
